cards.explanation: The answer is that they're filled with awe and run to greet Him. The text says, "As soon as all the people saw Jesus, they were filled with awe and ran to greet Him." (Mark 9:15) Picture it, friends. A crowd with scribes arguing in it, and the second they see Him, they take off running toward Him. I think the awe hit hard.

The answer is unable. The dad says, "I asked Your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable." (Mark 9:18) He doesn't say they refused or ran off. He says they couldn't do it. Later in the house, the disciples ask Jesus why, so they were wondering the same thing (Mark 9:28).

The answer is that Jesus says, "Bring the boy to Me." (Mark 9:19) Notice what He says right after asking how long He must put up with them. He asks for the boy. I think that's the best part of the verse, because the next thing He asks for is the one who needs help.

The answer is True. Mark 9:20 says, "So they brought him, and seeing Jesus, the spirit immediately threw the boy into a convulsion." The boy fell to the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth. It's a hard moment to hear, and I think this one hurts. Jesus is right there, though.

The answer is False. When Jesus asks how long this has been with the boy, the father says, "From childhood." (Mark 9:21) He doesn't say it only started recently. I think a dad who answers like that knows how heavy it gets.

The answer is "If You can." The dad says, "But if You can do anything…" and Jesus answers, "…if You can…" (Mark 9:22-23) He picks up those words and hands them right back. Then He says, "All things are possible to him who believes!" (Mark 9:23). I bet that echo gave the dad something to think about.

The answer is that he says he believes and asks for help with his unbelief, and I love how honest it is. The father cries out, "I do believe; help my unbelief!" (Mark 9:24) He doesn't dress it up. He says both parts out loud and asks Jesus for help with the second one. I think that's about as real a prayer as a person can pray.
The answer is False. Jesus tells the spirit, "I command you to come out and never enter him again." (Mark 9:25) There's no "maybe later" in that sentence. He closes the door behind it.

The answer is True. After the boy became like a corpse, Mark 9:27 says, "But Jesus took him by the hand and helped him to his feet, and he stood up." Look at that sequence, friends. Many were saying he was dead, and then Jesus' hand, and then the boy standing. I think that's a moment worth hearing twice.

The answer is prayer. Jesus says, "This kind cannot come out, except by prayer." (Mark 9:29) The disciples asked Him privately, and He gave them a straight answer. Short, simple, and worth keeping in the oven of your heart.
